title: Scientists Find the 'Chunkiest' Ancient Squid Relative
summary:
Two rare fossils from Wyoming show a new kind of ancient sea animal. It lived about 160 million years ago, in the Jurassic Period.

The animal is named Wyoteuthis linsterorum. It was a belemnite, a relative of today's squid and octopuses. Belemnites had a hard, bullet-shaped part inside their bodies called a rostrum. That part often turns into a fossil.

Most belemnite fossils in Wyoming are thin, only 1 to 2 centimeters wide. People there call them squid butts! The new one is about 6 centimeters wide, making it the thickest belemnite ever found. The whole animal may have been about two feet long.

The first fossil was found in the late 1990s and sat in a museum drawer for years. A second one was given to the Wyoming Dinosaur Center in 2019. Scientists used CT scans to look inside the fossils. Researcher Alexey Ippolitov thinks its big size may have helped it hunt smaller belemnites.
why_it_matters: It shows that even very common fossils can still hold big surprises for curious kids and scientists.
